relevant_findings.topic: EA-based unit of measure — per-door assembly
relevant_findings.finding: Exterior doors are counted as EA (each). Each door assembly is 1 EA regardless of physical size. The complexity dimension (single_slab, panel, grand_entry) drives time dramatically — from 1.0-2.0 hrs/EA for a new single slab to 5.0-10.0 hrs/EA for a grand entry with sidelites and transom. This is fundamentally different from SF-based or LF-based specs. Production rates are hours/EA, not SF/hr or LF/hr.

relevant_findings.topic: Three substrate materials with distinct coating requirements
relevant_findings.finding: Exterior doors come in three substrate materials: (1) Steel (hollow metal) — hot-rolled/cold-rolled/galvanized/galvannealed steel with internal stiffeners and foam cores. Seams create expansion joints that stress coatings. Requires DTM or zinc-rich epoxy primer. (2) Fiberglass — composite polymer mimicking wood, paint-grade or stain-grade. 100% acrylic latex ONLY — oil-based paints strictly prohibited due to outgassing blisters. (3) Wood — solid timber with floating panels, hygroscopic, highly susceptible to warping without six-side sealing.

relevant_findings.topic: Fiberglass doors require 100% acrylic only — oil-based prohibited
relevant_findings.finding: Fiberglass doors trap manufacturing vapors that release over years. Non-breathable oil-based coatings trap gas under sun heat, causing outgassing blisters — the #1 failure mode on fiberglass doors. Only 100% acrylic latex enamel (satin/semi-gloss/gloss) is permissible. The coating must be permeable to allow trapped gases to escape without blistering. Do NOT sand textured fiberglass doors — destroys the wood-grain profile.

relevant_findings.topic: IR-reflective coatings mandatory for dark colors (LRV < 30)
relevant_findings.finding: Colors with LRV < 30 on exterior doors require IR-reflective cool paint pigments (Complex Inorganic Color Pigments — CICPs). Drops surface temperature 20-30 degrees F. Without IR-reflective technology, dark colors cause: wood joint failure and warping, steel thermal expansion and joint separation, fiberglass outgassing acceleration. This is a HARD STOP for steel doors below LRV 30.

relevant_findings.topic: Six-side sealing mandate for wood doors
relevant_findings.finding: All six sides of a wood door must be finished within specified timeframes (2 weeks to 30 days per manufacturer). Rails (top/bottom ends) act as capillary networks — unsealed end-grain causes massive swelling and moisture wicking. Failure to seal = warranty voidance. The bottom edge is particularly critical and must be propped open during cure to avoid sticking.

relevant_findings.topic: Hardware removal is best practice — not tape-over
relevant_findings.finding: Best practice is total removal of all locking hardware, strike plates, hinges, address numbers, knockers, mail slots, doorbells before painting. Masking is discouraged because areas beneath hardware must be sealed to prevent moisture infiltration. Hardware removal/reinstall is a significant time component of door painting — estimated as a separate task.

Never paint weatherstripping — paint destroys elasticity, causes brittleness and seal tearing. Modern friction-fit stripping: gently pull out before painting, re-insert after finish is completely dry. If removal is impossible: push tape deep into gap between jamb and stripping with putty knife. This is a separate protection task.

relevant_findings.topic: Door complexity tiers drive production rate dramatically
relevant_findings.finding: Three complexity tiers: (1) single_slab — flat flush door, minimal detail, 1.0-2.0 hrs/EA new construction. (2) panel — raised panel door (2-6 panels), recessed panels require brush sequence (panels first, then stiles, then edges), 2.5-4.5 hrs/EA standard repaint (NC panel ~1.5-3.0 hrs/EA estimated). (3) grand_entry — door slab plus sidelites and transom, extensive glass masking, mullion painting, 5.0-10.0 hrs/EA. Grand entry may include 2-4 sidelite panels and transom window above.

relevant_findings.topic: DFT targets for exterior door systems
relevant_findings.finding: Standard exterior door system: 3.0-5.0 mils total DFT (typically 1.5 mils primer + 1.5-2.0 mils per finish coat). Verified with magnetic, eddy current, or ultrasonic gauges. Steel doors per ANSI A250.8 (SDI 100): maximum paint gloss = 20% reflectance (60-degree gloss meter) — high gloss emphasizes factory welding marks and surface imperfections.

relevant_findings.topic: Steel door surface preparation — solvent clean + degloss
relevant_findings.finding: Steel doors require solvent cleaning (xylene or acetone) + TSP detergent wash. Active oxidation requires power tool cleaning (SSPC-SP3) or commercial blast cleaning (SSPC-SP6) to bare metal. Scratches/rust spots: feather with 300-grit until transition is imperceptible. Dents: sand 80-grit, fill with 2-component body filler, finish-sand 240/300-grit. Factory-primed steel: degloss existing primer with light sand before topcoat or DTM primer.

relevant_findings.topic: Fiberglass door surface preparation — no sanding of textured surface
relevant_findings.finding: Fiberglass doors: clean with mild dish soap or denatured alcohol. NEVER use hydrocarbon-based solvents — damages resin. Do NOT sand textured (stain-grade) fiberglass doors — destroys the wood-grain profile. Paint-grade (smooth) fiberglass can be lightly scuffed for adhesion. Factory primer on fiberglass is typically compatible with 100% acrylic topcoat.

relevant_findings.topic: Spray-only application for door faces — back-rolling avoided
relevant_findings.finding: Per Application Methods Doctrine, metal doors should be spray-only — 'Orange peel from roller is undesirable.' Spray tip for metal doors and gutters: 0.010-0.014 inch orifice (310, 412 tip codes). Door faces are typically sprayed for factory-smooth finish quality. Brush is used only for panel recesses on raised-panel doors and edge details.

Primer by substrate: (1) Carbon steel = zinc-rich epoxy or alkyd (sacrificial barrier). (2) Galvanized/aluminum = vinyl wash or acrylic etching (chemical bond promotion). (3) Pre-primed/factory steel = universal acrylic DTM (compatibility). (4) Fiberglass = 100% acrylic latex primer (breathable, permeable). (5) Wood = acrylic latex exterior primer with alkyd spot-prime for tannin-rich species (cedar, redwood).

Paneled doors follow a specific sequence: recessed panels first, then stiles (middle, top, center, bottom), then vertical edges. This prevents lap marks and ensures complete coverage in panel recesses. For brush application: 1.5-2 inch angled sash brush for panel recesses, 2-2.5 inch for stiles and rails.

relevant_findings.topic: Sheen selection for exterior doors — semi-gloss or gloss
relevant_findings.finding: Valid sheens for exterior doors: satin, semi-gloss, gloss. Higher sheen adds durability on high-contact surfaces. No locked-in default — project-level selection. Semi-gloss and gloss are the most common choices for exterior entry doors due to dirt resistance, UV fade resistance, and visual impact. Steel doors per ANSI A250.8: caution with high gloss — emphasizes welding marks.

Caulking at the door casing-to-wall junction is the TRIM spec's responsibility (SF_TRIM_EXT_NC_v1), not the door spec. The door spec covers only the door slab, edges, and immediately adjacent components (glass lites, sidelites). Door-to-frame weatherseal gap is protected, not caulked. Any caulking of the door slab itself (e.g., panel joints on wood doors) is within this spec's scope.

relevant_findings.topic: Door edges — all four edges must be painted
relevant_findings.finding: All four edges of an exterior door must be painted: hinge edge, latch edge, top edge, and bottom edge. The bottom edge is critical for moisture protection (especially wood doors). Top and bottom edges are the primary moisture entry points. Hinge and latch edges require hardware removal first. Edge painting is done with brush regardless of face application method.

Grand entry door assemblies include: main door slab, sidelite panels (1-2 per side, typically fixed glass with painted mullions), transom window above (fixed glass with painted frame/mullions). Sidelites and transoms require extensive glass masking. Mullion and frame painting is detailed brush work. Total glass masking for a grand entry can add 1-3 hours depending on lite count.

condition_drivers.impact: Drives primer selection, surface prep protocol, topcoat chemistry restrictions, and failure mode profile. Steel = DTM primer, solvent clean. Fiberglass = 100% acrylic only, no oil, no sanding of texture. Wood = six-side sealing, tannin management, moisture cycling.
condition_drivers.notes: This is a CONFIGURATION DIMENSION — affects task structure, not just rate.

condition_drivers.impact: Determines prep depth and primer requirement. Bare wood = full prime + six-side seal. Bare metal = rust treatment + DTM primer. Factory-primed = degloss/scuff + topcoat (steel/fiberglass) or field prime (wood). Field-primed = direct topcoat.
condition_drivers.notes: SS_EXT_PRIMED_FACTORY is the dominant NC state for steel and fiberglass. SS_EXT_BARE_WOOD is dominant for wood doors.

condition_drivers.impact: Production rate varies dramatically: single_slab 1.0-2.0 hrs/EA, panel 1.5-3.0 hrs/EA (NC), grand_entry 5.0-10.0 hrs/EA. Grand entry adds sidelite/transom glass masking, mullion painting, and additional edge work. This is the primary cost driver.
condition_drivers.notes: This is a CONFIGURATION DIMENSION — changes task count and workflow.

condition_drivers.impact: QT3: standard 2-coat with clean edges. QT4: premium materials, light sand between coats. QT5: supreme — spray in controlled environment, hand-sand between coats, DFT verification. QT2 not applicable to exterior entry doors (architectural focal point).
condition_drivers.notes: QT5 is applicable to exterior doors because they are high-visibility architectural features.

condition_drivers.impact: Sheen is a project-level selection with no locked-in default. Higher sheen = more durable, cleanable, UV-resistant but reveals surface imperfections. Steel doors: caution with gloss per ANSI A250.8 (shows welding marks). Gloss requires higher prep quality.

Spray is primary for door faces (factory-smooth finish). Back-rolling AVOIDED on metal doors. Brush is used for: panel recesses, edges, detail work, and small projects where spray setup is not justified. Spray tip: 310 or 412 (0.010-0.014 inch orifice) for metal doors.
condition_drivers.notes: Brush_roll is not a valid option — roller introduces orange peel on door faces. Brush or spray only.

quality_differences.description: Standard exterior door. Clean and degloss (steel/fiberglass) or sand (wood). Primer per substrate. Two finish coats with mid-grade 100% acrylic exterior enamel. Clean edges at glass, hardware openings. Hardware removal and reinstall.

Premium exterior door. Same as QT3 plus: premium materials (SW Emerald, BM Aura). Light sand between finish coats (220-grit). Raking light inspection for runs, sags, holidays. Fill minor imperfections with glazing putty. Crisp glass-to-frame masking lines.

Supreme exterior door. Door removed from hinges, painted in controlled environment (garage/shop). Spray application with fine tip. Hand-sand between ALL coats (primer and finish). DFT verification with gauge. Glass masking with liquid mask for razor-sharp lines. Final coat applied with door hanging for gravity leveling.
quality_differences.typical_use: Grand entry doors, showcase homes, historic restoration.

failure_modes.name: Outgassing blisters on fiberglass
failure_modes.description: Trapped manufacturing vapors released over years. Non-breathable oil-based coatings trap gas under sun heat, causing blisters that erupt through the paint film.
failure_modes.prevention: Use ONLY 100% acrylic latex enamel on fiberglass doors. NEVER use oil-based or alkyd paints. Acrylic latex is permeable enough to allow trapped gases to escape without blistering.
failure_modes.detection: Blisters on sun-exposed fiberglass door face. Blisters contain air/gas, not liquid water.

failure_modes.name: Thermal warping from dark colors without IR-reflective
failure_modes.description: Low-LRV dark paint without IR-reflective properties causes excessive heat absorption. Steel doors: thermal expansion, joint separation, checking. Fiberglass: outgassing acceleration, softening. Wood: joint failure, panel warping.
failure_modes.prevention: HARD STOP: LRV < 30 AND high exposure = mandatory IR-reflective coating. IR-reflective pigments drop surface temperature 20-30 degrees F while maintaining dark visual appearance.
failure_modes.detection: Door warping, panel separation, joint opening, paint cracking at stress points.

failure_modes.name: Underfilm corrosion on steel
failure_modes.description: Rust painted over continues electrolytic action beneath the film. Moisture travels via capillary action under primer, spreading corrosion well beyond the visible rust area.
failure_modes.prevention: Remove ALL active rust to bare metal using SSPC-SP3 (power tool) or SSPC-SP6 (commercial blast). Apply zinc-rich epoxy or DTM primer to bare metal immediately. Never paint over active rust.
failure_modes.detection: Rust bleeding through paint. Blistering and lifting of paint film around rust spots.

failure_modes.name: Moisture wicking on wood doors — unsealed edges
failure_modes.description: Top and bottom rails act as capillary networks. Unsealed end-grain causes massive swelling, panel distortion, and joint failure. Bottom edge is the most critical — standing water and splash-back accelerate wicking.
failure_modes.prevention: Six-side sealing within manufacturer timeframe (2 weeks to 30 days). Seal ALL edges including top and bottom. Bottom edge: apply primer and finish, prop door open during cure.
failure_modes.detection: Swollen rails, panel distortion, paint cracking at joints, bottom edge swelling.

failure_modes.name: Adhesion failure from surface contamination — steel
failure_modes.description: Steel door surfaces contaminated with oils, waxes, or silicone release agents from manufacturing. Paint applied over contamination peels or delaminates.
failure_modes.prevention: Full solvent cleaning (xylene or acetone) + TSP detergent wash before primer application. Wipe test with clean white rag to verify decontamination.
failure_modes.detection: Paint peeling in sheets. Poor adhesion on scratch test. Fish-eye or crawling in wet film.

failure_modes.name: Caulk failure at panel joints — premature painting
failure_modes.description: Painting over uncured caulk at wood door panel joints. Caulk beads (~40 mils) shrink as they cure, cracking the 1-3 mil paint film.
failure_modes.prevention: Allow full cure per sealant type before painting. Acrylic latex: paint after skinning. Polyurethane: 3-7 day cure. Use flexible paintable caulk for wood door panel joints.
failure_modes.detection: Cracked paint over caulk joints. Visible caulk shrinkage.

primer_systems.name: Acrylic DTM (Direct-to-Metal) Primer
primer_systems.description: Universal acrylic DTM primer for compatibility with existing factory primer on steel doors. Provides adhesion bridge between factory primer and topcoat.
primer_systems.notes: Primary primer for factory-primed steel doors. Compatible with factory epoxy/zinc primers.

primer_systems.name: Zinc-Rich Epoxy Primer
primer_systems.description: Sacrificial barrier protection for bare carbon steel. Zinc particles corrode preferentially, protecting the steel substrate.
primer_systems.notes: Required for bare steel after SSPC-SP3/SP6 cleaning. Two-component system.

primer_systems.name: Vinyl Wash / Acrylic Etching Primer
primer_systems.description: Chemical bond promotion primer for galvanized or aluminum steel door components. Etches the passive zinc surface for adhesion.
primer_systems.notes: Required for galvanized steel surfaces. Quick dry time.

primer_systems.name: 100% Acrylic Latex Exterior Primer
primer_systems.description: Standard exterior primer for fiberglass and wood doors. Remains flexible long-term, breathable (critical for fiberglass outgassing management), good tannin blocking for most wood species.
primer_systems.notes: Primary primer for fiberglass and wood. For tannin-rich wood (cedar, redwood), supplement with alkyd spot-prime at knots.

primer_systems.name: Alkyd/Shellac Spot Primer
primer_systems.description: Spot-applied to visible wood knots on tannin-rich species before full acrylic primer coat. Superior tannin stain blocking.
primer_systems.notes: Knot spot-priming only — not full surface. Required for cedar/redwood/fir door species.

topcoat_systems.name: 100% Acrylic Latex Exterior Enamel
topcoat_systems.description: Standard exterior door finish. Superior UV resistance, flexibility for thermal movement, breathable (critical for fiberglass). Hard enamel finish for high-contact door surface.
topcoat_systems.notes: Mandatory chemistry for fiberglass doors. QT3: mid-grade (SW SuperPaint, BM Regal). QT4: premium (SW Emerald, BM Aura).

topcoat_systems.name: High-Build DTM Polyurethane/Polysiloxane Enamel
topcoat_systems.description: Premium topcoat for steel doors. Maximum UV resistance, abrasion resistance, and chemical resistance. High-build for superior DFT.
topcoat_systems.notes: Premium option for steel doors only. Not for fiberglass (permeability concern).

topcoat_systems.name: IR-Reflective Cool Paint Exterior Enamel
topcoat_systems.description: Infrared-reflective coating with Complex Inorganic Color Pigments (CICPs). Allows dark visual colors (LRV < 30) without excessive heat absorption. Drops surface temperature 20-30 degrees F.
topcoat_systems.notes: MANDATORY when color LRV < 30 and door has high sun exposure. Material cost premium over standard acrylic enamel.

notes_for_materials_manager: Fiberglass doors: 100% acrylic latex ONLY. Oil-based/alkyd paints are PROHIBITED — causes outgassing blisters.
Steel doors: DTM primer system. Factory-primed steel uses acrylic DTM over factory primer. Bare steel requires zinc-rich epoxy after SSPC cleaning.
Wood doors: 100% acrylic exterior primer. Alkyd spot-prime for tannin-rich species knots (cedar, redwood, fir).
IR-reflective coating: mandatory for LRV < 30 on any substrate. Material cost premium — track as separate material system variant.
Coverage rate for door surfaces: 300-400 SF/gal per coat (each door face is approximately 18-21 SF depending on size).
Spray tip for metal doors: 310 or 412 (0.010-0.014 inch orifice). 200-mesh red filter for enamel.
DFT target: 3.0-5.0 mils total (1.5 mils primer + 1.5-2.0 mils per finish coat).
Steel door gloss caution: per ANSI A250.8, high gloss emphasizes welding marks. Semi-gloss is safer default for steel.
Caulk for wood door panel joints: flexible paintable acrylic latex or siliconized acrylic. Polyurethane for expansion joints.
Grand entry components: additional masking materials — HDPE static-cling film for sidelite and transom glass, pre-taped poly for mullion masking.
notes_for_sop_librarian: Module structure: setup → protect → hardware_remove → clean → prep → prime → apply_coat_1 → sand_between (QT4/QT5) → apply_coat_2 → edge_seal (wood) → hardware_reinstall → cleanup → teardown.
Hardware removal is a SEPARATE TASK — not embedded in prep. Remove ALL hardware: lockset, deadbolt, strike plates, hinges, knocker, mail slot, doorbell, address numbers.
Weatherstrip protection: pull out friction-fit stripping before painting, re-insert after finish is dry. If non-removable: tape deep into gap with putty knife.
Six-side sealing for wood doors: ALL six sides must be sealed. Bottom edge: apply primer and finish, prop door open during cure. This is a conditional task (wood substrate only).
Paneled door sequence: recessed panels first, then stiles (middle, top, center, bottom), then vertical edges. Prevents lap marks.
Fiberglass prep: NEVER sand textured surfaces. Clean with mild soap or denatured alcohol. NEVER use hydrocarbon solvents.
Steel prep: solvent clean (xylene/acetone) + TSP wash. Active rust: power tool clean (SSPC-SP3). Dents: 80-grit sand, 2-part body filler, finish-sand 240/300-grit.
Spray application for door faces — back-rolling AVOIDED on metal doors (introduces orange peel).
Grand entry module: additional tasks for sidelite/transom glass masking, mullion painting, additional edge work at sidelite-to-slab frame junction.
Light sand between coats: QT4 with 220-grit. QT5 with 220-320 grit and raking light inspection.
Bottom edge cure: prop door open (wood block or wedge) during bottom seal cure to prevent sticking to threshold.
IR-reflective coating task: conditional on LRV < 30. Switches topcoat material system to SYS_FINISH_IR_REFLECTIVE.
notes_for_estimation_engineer: This is an EA-BASED spec. Production rates are hours/EA, NOT SF/hr or LF/hr.
Production rates by complexity (NEW CONSTRUCTION): single_slab = 1.0-2.0 hrs/EA, panel = 1.5-3.0 hrs/EA, grand_entry = 5.0-10.0 hrs/EA.
Hardware removal/reinstall: 0.25-0.50 hrs/EA (single lockset + deadbolt). Grand entry hardware: 0.50-1.0 hrs/EA.
Glass masking: single lite = 0.10-0.15 hrs/EA. Grand entry (sidelites + transom): 0.75-2.0 hrs/EA depending on lite count.
Six-side seal (wood only): adds 0.25-0.50 hrs/EA over standard 2-face painting — edges are brush work regardless of face method.
Door edge painting: included in per-EA rate, not a separate line item. All 4 edges painted with brush.
Substrate material modifier: steel = 1.00 (baseline), fiberglass = 0.90 (less prep), wood = 1.15 (six-side seal + grain management).
Access is typically ground-level for exterior doors (no height modifier). Exception: if door is elevated (deck/porch entry with scaffolded access).
Environmental conditions (wind, temp, dew point) are EXCLUDED from estimation — SOP concerns only.
Coat system: 1 primer + 2 finish coats standard at all QTs for NC. SS_EXT_PRIMED_FIELD skips prime.
IR-reflective coating upcharge: material cost modifier only — does not affect labor rate.
Grand entry rate includes sidelite/transom work as part of the assembly. Do not double-count with a separate window spec.

assumptions.value: New construction exterior entry doors only — single slab through grand entry with sidelites/transom. Does not include: garage doors (separate spec SF_GARAGE_DOOR_EXT_NC_v1), interior face of exterior doors (covered by interior door spec), door casing/trim (covered by SF_TRIM_EXT_NC_v1).
assumptions.note: Door casing painting belongs to the trim spec. This spec covers: door slab (both exterior and interior faces when exterior door is fully scoped), door edges (4), sidelites and transom (grand_entry complexity only), hardware removal/reinstall.

assumptions.value: QT2 not applicable to exterior entry doors
assumptions.note: Exterior entry doors are high-visibility architectural focal points. QT3 is the minimum standard. No economy tier.

assumptions.value: Repaint substrate states excluded from this NC spec
assumptions.source: User brief — 'New construction exterior entry doors'
assumptions.note: Repaint adds 30-100% labor premium (Exterior_Doors_Doctrine.md §4). Requires separate spec with fundamentally different prep modules.

assumptions.value: Both exterior and interior faces of the exterior door are in scope
assumptions.source: Standard painting practice — exterior doors are painted on both faces during NC
assumptions.note: Doctrine does not explicitly state whether interior face is in scope. Standard NC practice is to paint both faces. Confirm with Eric.

assumptions.value: Spray is primary for door faces, brush for edges and panel recesses. No roller option.
assumptions.note: Metal doors: spray only, no back-roll. Fiberglass: spray preferred, brush acceptable. Wood panels: spray face + brush panel recesses.

uncertainties.topic: Interior face of exterior door — scope ownership
uncertainties.detail: Doctrine does not explicitly state whether the interior face of the exterior door is scoped under this exterior door spec or the interior door spec. Standard NC practice paints both faces during exterior door installation. This needs confirmation.
uncertainties.recommendation: Confirm with Eric. If interior face is in scope, production rates should reflect 2-face painting (already included in the EA rates from doctrine). If not, rates need adjustment.

uncertainties.detail: Grand entry rate range is very wide (5.0-10.0 hrs/EA). The low end assumes standard sidelites with simple glass. The high end assumes elaborate mullion patterns, leaded glass, transom with multiple lites. Lite count is the primary variable but doctrine does not provide per-lite rate calibration.
uncertainties.recommendation: Use glass lite count as a sub-modifier within grand_entry complexity. Estimate 0.15-0.25 hrs per individual lite for masking + mullion painting.

uncertainties.topic: Stain-grade fiberglass door — gel stain path
uncertainties.detail: Exterior_Doors_Doctrine.md §3 mentions 'Substrate = Fiberglass AND Finish = Stain → Trigger gel stain + clear topcoat requirement.' This spec covers PAINT finish only. Gel stain + clear topcoat is a fundamentally different workflow that may require a separate spec (SF_DOOR_EXT_NC_STAIN_v1).
uncertainties.recommendation: Exclude stain-grade fiberglass finishing from this spec. Document as future spec if demand warrants.

uncertainties.detail: Doctrine provides 2.5-4.5 hrs/EA for 'standard repaint' panel doors. NC panel doors should be faster (no scraping/feathering). Estimated NC rate at 1.5-3.0 hrs/EA based on removing the 30-100% repaint premium. This is an inference, not a doctrine-calibrated rate.
uncertainties.recommendation: Flag NC panel rates for field calibration. Use 1.5-3.0 hrs/EA as starting estimate.

zones.notes: Glass lites in door slab. HDPE static-cling masking film or liquid mask. Single lite per standard door. Grand entry: multiple lites in sidelites/transom.
Best practice is FULL REMOVAL of all hardware — lockset, deadbolt, strike plates, hinges, knocker, mail slot, doorbell, address numbers. Masking is discouraged per doctrine.
Pull out friction-fit weatherstripping before painting. If non-removable, push tape deep into gap. No PaintScope key — counted per door (1 EA per door).
Threshold/sill protection from drips during door painting. Tape and drop cloth. No separate PaintScope key — included in per-door setup.

zones.upgrade_scenario: Upgrades to full_cover when application_method = spray
zones.notes: Entry walkway/porch/stoop at door base. Drop cloth for drips (brush), full tarp for overspray (spray).

protection_zones_analysis.cross_spec_protection_note: Door casing protection (from siding spray) is NOT this spec's responsibility — belongs to siding or trim spec. Door glass masking IS this spec's responsibility when the door is being painted.

adjacent_surfaces.notes: Door casing trim surrounds the door opening. Different color/sheen from door slab. Casing is painted by SF_TRIM_EXT_NC_v1. No cut-in required — hardware removal exposes the full edge.
Door frame/jamb is typically painted the same color as the door. Frame painting is included in the per-door EA rate. Jamb faces are brush work.
Glass lites in door slab or sidelites/transom. Protection target — masked, not painted. Mullion frames between lites are painted.
Siding terminates at door casing. No direct adjacency between door slab and siding — casing intervenes.

adjacency_analysis.key_finding: Door slab has minimal edge work because hardware removal exposes all surfaces. Frame/jamb painting is included in the per-EA rate. Glass lites are protection targets only. Casing belongs to the trim spec.

affected_conditions.notes: Exterior doors are typically at ground level. Height modifier only applies when door is on elevated deck/porch requiring ladder access. Scaffold/lift not typically needed for door painting.

excluded_conditions.rationale: Environmental conditions are unpredictable at bid time. They are SOP/process concerns, not estimatable. Per fiber cement and trim sibling spec pattern.

excluded.reason: Unpredictable. Spray doors in sheltered conditions or remove door to shop.
Varies by time of day. Dark door faces get very hot in direct sun — schedule for shade.
Weather-dependent. Not predictable at bid time.
Affects drying and IR-reflective coating requirement but not production rate.

valid_input_states.rationale: NC exterior doors arrive in one of these four states. Steel and fiberglass doors are typically factory-primed. Wood doors may be bare or factory-primed depending on manufacturer. Field-primed means primer already applied on-site — ready for topcoat.

output_state.rationale: Output state is the painted finish. Semi-gloss is the most common exterior door sheen. Actual output varies by project sheen selection (satin, semi-gloss, gloss).

adjacent_state_protection_analysis.rationale: Protect finished casing from door painting overspray. Minimal risk — door is typically painted after casing. If casing is unfinished, no protection needed.
No direct adjacency — casing intervenes between door slab and siding. Casing provides natural separation.

exterior_substrate_states.description: Raw uncoated wood door — no primer, no stain, no finish.
exterior_substrate_states.prep_requirements: Sand to remove mill glaze (120-grit). Fill defects with exterior wood filler. Clean. Spot-prime knots on tannin-rich species (cedar, redwood).
exterior_substrate_states.primer_type: 100% acrylic latex exterior primer. Alkyd spot-prime for knots on tannin-rich species.
exterior_substrate_states.notes: Six-side sealing mandatory. All edges (including top and bottom) must be primed and finished within manufacturer timeframe.

exterior_substrate_states.description: Raw ferrous or non-ferrous metal door — no primer, no coating. Exposed after rust removal or new unpainted metal.
exterior_substrate_states.prep_requirements: Solvent clean (xylene/acetone) + TSP wash. Active rust: SSPC-SP3 (power tool) or SSPC-SP6 (blast clean) to bare metal. Dents: body filler + finish-sand.
exterior_substrate_states.primer_type: Carbon steel = zinc-rich epoxy or alkyd. Galvanized = vinyl wash or acrylic etching primer.
exterior_substrate_states.notes: Rare in NC — most steel doors arrive factory-primed. This state occurs when factory primer is damaged or door is unpainted.

exterior_substrate_states.description: Factory-applied primer on steel or fiberglass door.
exterior_substrate_states.prep_requirements: Light degloss/scuff with 220-grit (steel). Clean surface with denatured alcohol or mild soap (fiberglass). Inspect for damage, spot-repair.
exterior_substrate_states.primer_type: None for steel/fiberglass — factory primer is adequate adhesion base. Optional DTM primer for steel if factory primer is degraded.
exterior_substrate_states.notes: Dominant NC state for steel and fiberglass doors. Factory primer on these substrates IS a suitable base for topcoat (unlike fiber cement siding where field prime over factory prime is mandatory).

exterior_substrate_states.description: Field-applied exterior primer — ready for topcoat.
exterior_substrate_states.prep_requirements: Light dust-off. Minimal prep — surface is paint-ready.
exterior_substrate_states.notes: Occurs when prime and finish are split across mobilizations. Direct topcoat application.

exterior_access_type_analysis.treatment: Rarely applicable. Exterior doors are typically at ground level.

scenarios.notes: Standard entry door at grade. Baseline rate. Most common scenario.
Elevated entry (deck, raised porch). Minor height modifier — door is still a compact workspace.

exterior_environmental_constraints.note: Environmental constraints documented for SOP reference only — EXCLUDED from estimation modifiers.

sop_reference_only.note: Doors can be removed and sprayed in sheltered area (garage/shop) to avoid wind issues.
Dark door faces absorb significant heat in direct sun. Schedule painting for shade hours.

sop_reference_only.rule: Surface temp must be >= 5°F above dew point
sop_reference_only.note: Adhesion and blushing risk on metal substrates.

sop_reference_only.rule: Prop door open during bottom edge cure — avoid contact with threshold
sop_reference_only.note: Bottom edge sticking is a common failure on wood doors.

single_slab_spray.notes: Flat flush door, spray face + brush edges. NC new door. Includes both faces and all 4 edges.

panel_spray.notes: Raised panel door (2-6 panels), spray face + brush panel recesses and edges. NC new door. Inferred from repaint rate 2.5-4.5 minus 30% repaint premium.

grand_entry_spray.notes: Door slab + sidelites + transom. Includes glass masking, mullion painting, all edges. Wide range — lite count is primary variable.

hardware_remove_reinstall.notes: Standard door: lockset + deadbolt + strike plates. Grand entry: 0.50-1.0 hrs/EA for additional hardware.

glass_masking_single_lite.notes: Per lite masking with HDPE film or liquid mask. Grand entry glass masking included in grand_entry rate.

weatherstrip_protect.notes: Pull and re-insert friction-fit stripping, or deep tape.

six_side_seal_wood.notes: Additional time for wood door edge painting (all 4 edges + attention to bottom seal). Brush work.

prep_fiberglass_factory_primed.notes: Soap wash, inspect. No sanding of textured surfaces.

prep_wood_bare.notes: Sand mill glaze, fill defects, spot-prime knots. More intensive than factory-primed substrates.

key_decisions.decision: This spec uses EA (each door assembly) as the primary UOM, not SF or LF.
key_decisions.rationale: Exterior doors are discrete architectural units. The PS key is PS_EXT_OPENING_EA.DOOR_EXT. Complexity dimension (single_slab/panel/grand_entry) drives time within the EA. Grand entry includes sidelites and transom as part of the assembly — not counted separately.

key_decisions.decision: Combined (full phase_scope). Prime and finish phases have unique task keys within the single spec.
key_decisions.rationale: NC exterior doors are a single-mobilization scope — same crew primes and paints. Each phase (prime, finish) has its own task IDs and module IDs. Matches sibling exterior spec pattern.

key_decisions.decision: substrate_material (steel/fiberglass/wood) is a CONFIGURATION DIMENSION — changes task structure, primer system, and topcoat chemistry.
key_decisions.rationale: Each substrate requires fundamentally different prep, primer, and topcoat. Fiberglass prohibits oil-based. Steel requires DTM. Wood requires six-side seal. These are workflow branches, not rate modifiers.

key_decisions.decision: door_complexity (single_slab/panel/grand_entry) is a CONFIGURATION DIMENSION — changes rate and may add/remove tasks.
key_decisions.rationale: Grand entry adds sidelite/transom tasks (glass masking, mullion painting) that do not exist for single_slab or panel. Rate ranges are non-overlapping. This is a task-structure branch.

key_decisions.decision: QT2 is NOT applicable to exterior entry doors.
key_decisions.rationale: Exterior entry doors are high-visibility architectural focal points. QT3 is the minimum standard. No economy tier for entry doors.

key_decisions.decision: QT5 IS applicable to exterior entry doors.
key_decisions.rationale: Grand entry doors and showcase entries justify QT5 (supreme) — door removed, painted in controlled environment, hand-sand between all coats, DFT verification. Exterior doors are one of the few exterior elements that warrant QT5.

key_decisions.decision: Hardware REMOVAL is the standard approach. Masking is not offered as an alternative.
key_decisions.rationale: Per Exterior_Doors_Doctrine.md §6: 'Best practice: Total removal of all locking hardware, strike plates, hinges, address numbers before painting.' Areas beneath hardware must be sealed. Masking prevents proper sealing.

key_decisions.decision: Valid application methods are spray and brush. Roller is NOT a valid option for door faces.
key_decisions.rationale: Per Application Methods Doctrine: 'Metal doors: Spray-only for smooth finish.' Roller introduces orange peel. Brush is acceptable for fiberglass/wood but spray is preferred for quality.

key_decisions.decision: Door casing painting belongs to SF_TRIM_EXT_NC_v1, NOT this spec.
key_decisions.rationale: Per trim spec pattern. Casing is a trim component. This spec covers: door slab (faces + edges), frame/jamb, glass lite masking, hardware removal/reinstall, and sidelite/transom painting (grand entry).

key_decisions.decision: EXCLUDED from estimation modifiers. Per sibling spec pattern.
key_decisions.rationale: Environmental conditions are unpredictable at bid time. They belong in SOP procedure notes, not production rate modifiers.

key_decisions.decision: Gel stain + clear topcoat workflow for stain-grade fiberglass doors is OUT OF SCOPE.
key_decisions.rationale: This spec covers PAINT finish only. Gel stain is a fundamentally different workflow (stain application + clear topcoat) that requires a separate spec if demand warrants.

key_decisions.decision: 1 primer + 2 finish coats standard at all tiers for NC. SS_EXT_PRIMED_FIELD skips prime. SS_EXT_PRIMED_FACTORY may skip prime for steel/fiberglass (factory primer adequate).
key_decisions.rationale: DFT target 3.0-5.0 mils requires primer + 2 finish coats. Factory-primed steel/fiberglass doors have adequate factory primer base unlike fiber cement siding where field prime is mandatory.

proposed_new_keys.rationale: Door complexity is the primary cost driver for this EA-based spec. PaintScope must capture this classification during scope capture to route to correct production rate tier. Not derivable from other keys.
proposed_new_keys.alternative: Could be captured as a project-level configuration dimension instead of a PaintScope key. But PaintScope capture is preferred because it can vary per door within a project (e.g., front entry is grand_entry, side entry is single_slab).

proposed_new_keys.rationale: Substrate material drives primer system, topcoat chemistry restrictions, and prep protocol. Must be captured per door because a project can have mixed substrates (e.g., steel front door, fiberglass side door).
proposed_new_keys.alternative: Could be a project-level default with per-door override.
